definitions.explanation: Addressing the root cause of a problem rather than surface symptoms. Used to describe reforms, changes, or solutions that go to the very foundation of an issue.

examples.japanese: {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な⟦{解決|かいけつ}→解決：00136_kaiketsu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦まだ→まだ：00603_mada⟧⟦{時間|じかん}がかかる→時間がかかる：26082_jikangakakaru⟧。
examples.english: It will still take time to achieve a fundamental solution to the problem.

examples.japanese: ⟦{制度|せいど}→制度：03291_seido⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{抜本的|ばっぽんてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{見直|みなお}さなければ→見直す：04579_minaosu⟧、⟦{同|おな}じ→同じ：02857_onaji⟧⟦{問題|もんだい}→問題：00797_mondai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{繰|く}り{返|かえ}される→繰り返す：02051_kurikaesu⟧だろう。
examples.english: Unless the system is fundamentally re-examined, the same problems will recur.

notes:
USAGE:
Literally means "pulling out the root" (⟦{抜|ぬ}く→抜く：02384_nuku⟧ = pull out, {本|もと} = root/origin). Used as a na-adjective, almost always with な or ⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧. Frequently appears in formal contexts such as political speeches, news reports, and policy discussions. Implies that half-measures are insufficient and deep structural change is required.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な⟦{改革|かいかく}→改革：04815_kaikaku⟧: fundamental reform
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な⟦{見直|みなお}し→見直し：09340_minaoshi⟧: fundamental review
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}な⟦{対策|たいさく}→対策：02511_taisaku⟧: drastic measures
- {抜本的|ばっぽんてき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{変|か}える→変える：01089_kaeru⟧: to change fundamentally

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{根本的|こんぽんてき}→根本的：17920_konponteki⟧: fundamental (similar but broader; less reform-oriented)
- ⟦{徹底的|てっていてき}→徹底的：06827_tetteiteki⟧: thorough (emphasizes completeness rather than depth)
